question: Add a DAF-to-DAF netting rule (R5) to the corrected DAFRC market totals: subtract Schedule I lines from every panel sponsor to DAF-holding panel recipients (FY2021-FY2024) from both aggregate grants and contributions, with a lower bound restricted to national/processor recipients and an audit-based check of what share of lines to community foundations land in DAFs rather than other funds
conclusion_affected: Market contributions, grants and payout rate; growth rates
rationale: Panel-wide Schedule I lines to DAF-holding sponsors were $5.24bn (FY2023) and $9.56bn (FY2024), 9.6% and 14.8% of DAFRC grants and 8.0% and 10.6% of contributions, counted on both sides. Top-50 pair flows net to 51% of gross. The cached extracts already hold every line, so the rule is mechanical

question: Replace DAFRC 'closed' flags and imputations for sponsors that still answer Part IV line 6 Yes with Schedule D Part I blank, using audited statements from state charity registries for the largest cases (Truman Heartland, Give2Asia, Jewish CF 470874376, Tompkins, Kern, CF of Middle Tennessee FY2021-22, Christian Community Foundation FY2022-23 and FY2025, Walker Area CF)
conclusion_affected: Exit-rate bounds (now 0.91% central, 0.99% upper); DAFRC imputed balances
rationale: 185 blank returns from 113 DAFRC sponsors: 31 sponsors dropped as closed (carry-forward $151-172m a year in FY2023-24) and 62 imputed ($1.60bn over FY2021-24). Audits would turn carry-forward proxies into measured balances and settle 11 tier-C exits that now look like reporting gaps

question: For the line-3 focus hits with normal total returns (MS GIFT, Foundation for the Carolinas, Foundation for the Charlotte Jewish Community, Endaoment FY2024), read audited statements or annual reports to test whether dividends and interest are booked inside pooled-unit gains (classification) or reduced by account-level fees (netting), and quantify any netted fee layer
conclusion_affected: Whether Part IX understates donor-borne cost at broker captives
rationale: The universe screen found MS GIFT is the only broker or bank captive under 50 bps (next: GS Charitable Gift Fund 67 bps, Bessemer 94-159). FFTC (28-34 bps) and the Charlotte Jewish foundation (23-26 bps) show the same low line 3 with normal 1,000-1,700 bps total returns, which points to classification rather than fees.
